items.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013
items.q: Ingrid Jensen is a very good trumpet player, Virginia Mayhew is an excellent tenor player, and they have groups that are otherwise male in most cases, so women have also — Anat has a quartet and they’re all guys except her.

ctx.x: Well it’s a good question, I’m glad you asked it, because it is something that is on my mind. We know that historically there’ve been certain important women in jazz — certainly the singers, but then there’s Mary Lou Williams who is always brought up as the great female arranger, composer and instrumentalist. But although there were some very talented women, a lot of piano players but also horn players, it really was a minority. I remember seeing — Charlie Shavers brought a group into a little club in New York…

attractive lady. And she played great bass. But that was such a novelty. And today fortunately we have a lot more talented and fairly prominent women in jazz. I mean I was a big fan of hers anyway but I was very happy when Anat Cohen started winning the clarinet thing in the DownBeat Critics Poll and has won it over a number of years.
